test_title: PYST 19: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 18th_September_2025_Shift_1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements correctly applies the weighted voting mechanism under Article 279A(9) of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: The Centre holds 75% of the voting power in the GST Council.
A GST Council decision can be passed solely with the support of the Centre and one State.
The States collectively have twice the voting weight of the Centre in the GST Council.
Each State has equal weightage as the Centre in GST Council voting.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The States collectively have twice the voting weight of the Centre in the GST Council.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 279A of the Indian Constitution establishes the GST Council, which is a federal body tasked with making key decisions related to the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
 
• The voting structure in the GST Council is designed to balance the interests of the Centre and States.
 
• As per Article 279A(9), the Centre holds a voting weight of one-third (33.33%) of the total votes.
 
• The States collectively hold two-thirds (66.67%) of the total voting weight in the GST Council.
 
• A decision in the GST Council requires a three-fourths (75%) majority of the weighted votes, ensuring that the States play a significant role in decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: The Centre holds 75% of the voting power in the GST Council**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect as the Centre holds only one-third (33.33%) of the total voting power in the GST Council.
 
• The remaining two-thirds (66.67%) of the voting power is collectively held by the States.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: A GST Council decision can be passed solely with the support of the Centre and one State**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect as decisions in the GST Council require a three-fourths (75%) majority of the weighted votes.
 
• Since the Centre has only one-third (33.33%) of the voting power, it cannot pass a decision unilaterally or with the support of just one State.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Each State has equal weightage as the Centre in GST Council voting**
 
 
• This statement is also incorrect. While each State has equal voting power among themselves, the collective weightage of all States is two-thirds (66.67%), which is twice that of the Centre's one-third (33.33%).
 
• The Centre does not hold equal voting weight as an individual State; instead, its voting weight is predefined as one-third of the total.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: GST Council and Its Voting Mechanism**
 
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body formed under Article 279A to make recommendations on various aspects of GST, such as tax rates, exemptions, and procedural rules.
 
• The council consists of the Union Finance Minister as the Chairperson, the Union Minister of State for Finance, and State Finance Ministers.
 
• The unique voting structure ensures cooperative federalism by giving States a collective upper hand while maintaining the Centre's significant say in decisions.
